correctness.rationale: Exact determinant recurrence gives the complete shadow fibre: four positive squared weights have sum S=1+q and matching quadratic Q=q. For fixed maximum cap t, eliminate two variables to obtain Q_min=2St-5t^2 for S/4<=t<=S/3 and Q_min=t(S-2t) for S/3<=t<=S/2. Solving q=Q_min gives the two lower-q branches and a sharp nonattainment boundary at q*=(7-3sqrt(5))/2. A 3x2 bipartite singular-value test yields q<=max(x1,x4)<=t; equality is attainable exactly from q>=1/3 and forces x1=x4=q. All equality cases are derived algebraically; a strict positive sequence approaches the unattained boundary exactly preserving both invariants. The standalone supplementary checker passed 3817 cases and does not replace any infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete numerical shadow is a natural distributional inverse datum. The exact smallest possible norm in its first two-dimensional strictly positive nilpotent-shift fibre is a quantitative identifiability invariant. Two different sharp thresholds distinguish nonattainment, two optimal allocations, a unique symmetric allocation, and a continuous optimizer family. These are mathematical structural features, not mere normalization checks or numerical refinements.
